Jack Henry Expands Collaboration With Google Cloud to Deliver Tokenized Deposits for Banks and Credit Unions
summary:
Jack Henry® today announced an expansion of its collaboration with Google Cloud designed to pave the way for banks and credit unions to offer tokenized deposits through Google Cloud Universal Ledger (GCUL). As part of the expanding relationship, Jack Henry will become the first core technology provider to integrate with GCUL, helping financial institutions modernize deposit offerings, strengthen accountholder relationships, and introduce new payment and settlement capabilities. GCUL is a fully managed, distributed ledger service that enables financial institutions to tokenize and transfer money and assets on a shared, real-time record with programmable, 24/7 settlement capabilities.
As consumer and business expectations continue to evolve toward real-time, programmable, and seamless financial experiences, community and regional financial institutions face growing competition from large banks and fintech providers. By integrating tokenized deposit infrastructure into Jack Henry's ecosystem, banks and credit unions can explore new transactional use cases, enhance digital experiences, and position themselves to meet emerging market demands.
"Tokenized deposits have the potential to reshape how money moves across the financial ecosystem," said Jack Henry Chief Technology Officer Ben Metz. "Our strategy is centered on helping financial institutions navigate emerging technologies and access innovative capabilities through trusted, scalable infrastructure. By expanding our work with Google Cloud and serving as the first core technology provider to use GCUL, we're helping community banks and credit unions explore new opportunities while building on the relationships, service, and expertise that have always set them apart."
Jack Henry and Google Cloud established their strategic relationship in 2022 to accelerate Jack Henry's cloud-native technology modernization strategy. Last June, the companies announced plans to deliver AI-driven security capabilities, integrating Google Cloud's agentic defense solutions to protect banks and credit unions against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. The integration with GCUL combines modern ledger technology with secure, scalable cloud infrastructure to help financial institutions explore new digital asset and payment capabilities.
"Financial innovation should be accessible to institutions of all sizes," said James Tromans, director, Web3 and Digital Assets at Google Cloud. "Google Cloud Universal Ledger provides a secure and scalable foundation for programmable value exchange. Through our collaboration with Jack Henry, we are bringing advanced digital asset capabilities to community and regional financial institutions, helping them build on the relationships and trust they have established with their customers."

title: Fiserv Simplifies Cross-Border Commerce With Commerce Hub™
summary:
Fiserv, Inc. , a leading global provider of payments and financial services technology solutions, today announced the global availability of Commerce Hub, a platform that enables enterprise merchants to orchestrate and simplify commerce through a single connection to Fiserv's commerce capabilities.
Commerce Hub currently supports more than several billions in processing and growing more than 100% YOY across multiple industries, payment methods and business models, supporting enterprises ranging spanning global marketplaces and platforms, to traditional brick-and-mortar and advanced, specialized sectors including grocery, petroleum and restaurants. Built to help businesses simplify and scale commerce operations, Commerce Hub brings together payment optimization, orchestration, and value-added services in a single platform, enabling clients to improve performance, streamline operations, and deliver consistent commerce experiences across markets.
As businesses pursue growth across borders, they often face a mix of payment providers, fragmented integration, local payment methods, and evolving regulatory considerations that create operational complexities and costs. Commerce Hub simplifies global commerce by providing access to market-specific payment options, acquiring services and value-added capabilities through a single platform, helping businesses scale more efficiently while maintaining a consistent operating model across markets. Combining Fiserv’s global reach with deep local market expertise, Commerce Hub enables businesses to launch faster, optimize performance and gain greater visibility across their commerce operations globally.
Through Commerce Hub, merchants can access:
One global connection: A single integration for onboarding, APIs, reporting, and operational controls for Fiserv merchant services.
Local commerce capabilities at a global scale: Access to local payment methods, acquiring, settlement options, and regional expertise that help businesses meet customer expectations in every market.
Scalable infrastructure: Cloud-native technology designed to streamline integrations and accelerate the delivery of new commerce capabilities.
Integrated value-added services: Payment optimization, fraud protection, cross-border capabilities, and support for emerging payment methods from a unified platform.
“Growth shouldn't be constrained by payment complexity,” said Lia Cao, Chief Revenue Officer, Enterprise and Platforms, at Fiserv. “Commerce Hub simplifies cross-border expansion by bringing together global scale, local expertise and value-added services on a single platform. We're helping clients expand faster, operate more efficiently, and deliver great customer experiences wherever they do business.”
Extending Global Commerce Strategy with Commerce Hub
Dell Technologies is among the global enterprises leveraging Commerce Hub to support a more unified approach to commerce. Dell's experience using Commerce Hub to introduce PIX in Brazil reflects how businesses can adapt to local customer preferences while keeping operations consistent at scale.

title: Finastra Launches Cloud-Enabled SBLC Solution to Help U.S. Banks Digitize Standby Letter of Credit Processing
summary:
Today at Money 20/20 in Las Vegas, Finastra announced Finastra StandbyX, a cloud-enabled solution designed to help U.S. banks digitize and automate standby letter of credit (SBLC) processing while strengthening risk management and operational efficiency.
 
SBLCs remain a widely used instrument across both trade and non-trade transactions in the U.S. While larger institutions typically manage SBLCs, alongside broader trade finance operations on platforms such as Trade Innovation, many regional and mid-sized banks continue to rely on manual or semi-manual processes. This can create operational inefficiencies, increase risk, and limit scalability.
 
Purpose-built for SBLCs, Finastra StandbyX provides a streamlined SaaS deployment model that enables banks to modernize their operations without implementing a full trade finance platform. Designed for rapid implementation, the solution minimizes integration requirements and testing effort while offering a competitive total cost of ownership.
 
The launch forms part of Finastra’s ongoing investment in its trade solutions portfolio, helping financial institutions modernize operations, improve efficiency, unlock new growth opportunities, and deliver better customer and user experiences.
 
How Finastra StandbyX helps banks in the U.S.
 


Provides proven standby letter of credit capabilities, through the SBLC module of Finastra’s Trade Innovation platform, which is trusted by more than 150 banks globally, helping institutions digitize operations, support growth, and strengthen risk management.
Offers a SaaS deployment model that enables banks with low to moderate transaction volumes to implement quickly and begin realizing value sooner.
Reduces operational complexity through streamlined integration and testing requirements.
It is backed by Finastra’s decades of experience supporting mission-critical banking systems for financial institutions worldwide.
Expert perspective: Digital trade for more banks
 

“Many U.S. banks have traditionally managed standby letters of credit through manual processes or workarounds," said Vinay Mendonca, Head of Trade and Supply Chain Finance and Corporate Channels at Finastra. While transaction volumes may be relatively low, the value of these instruments is often significant, making effective risk management essential. Finastra StandbyX gives banks access to proven SaaS technology that digitizes SBLC processing without the need to deploy a full trade finance platform. By making trade finance technology more accessible, we are helping a broader range of institutions improve operational efficiency, strengthen controls, and deliver a better customer experience. This is an exciting step in the evolution of our trade proposition."
 
Finastra StandbyX builds on the proven capabilities of Trade Innovation, Finastra’s trade finance platform that helps financial institutions automate workflows, manage risk, and improve operational efficiency. As part of Finastra's strategy to deliver modular, cloud-enabled and API-first solutions, StandbyX extends access to digital trade functionality for a wider range of banks.

Fission Raises $10M Series A Led by Pantera Capital to Bring Liquidity to Digital Private Markets
summary:
Fission, a blockchain-enabled financial technology company building liquidity infrastructure for tokenized investment funds, today announced it has closed a $10 million Series A funding round led by Pantera Capital and backed by a group of investors spanning traditional finance and digital assets.
Investment funds are rapidly moving on-chain. Tokenization has already transformed how fund interests can be issued, distributed and settled, but much of the underlying market structure remains unchanged. Tokenized funds still rely on periodic redemption windows, limited secondary liquidity and restrictive financing structures.
Fission is building the liquidity layer designed to change that.
The company enables investor liquidity for supported tokenized fund products, allowing eligible holders to access capital without waiting for traditional fund redemption cycles. Fission supports a growing universe of tokenized funds across asset classes including private credit, alternatives and other institutional investment products. The company has already processed millions of dollars in transactions and is expanding its capacity through both traditional and on-chain sources of capital.
"Putting funds on-chain is only the beginning," said Jonathan Shaffer, Founder and CEO of Fission. "The real promise of tokenization is creating fundamentally better markets around these assets: broader distribution, continuous liquidity and the ability to use fund interests as collateral in lending markets. Whether a fund is private or simply constrained by traditional liquidity structures, Fission is building the technology that makes those assets more liquid, transferable and useful across financial markets."
Fission's platform is purpose-built for institutional and permissioned markets, with infrastructure designed around the investor eligibility, transfer restrictions and compliance requirements governing regulated investment products. This allows Fission to bring on-chain liquidity to these assets while preserving the controls required by securities markets.
The new capital will support Fission's continued expansion across asset coverage, liquidity capacity and institutional integrations.
"Investment funds are moving onto digital rails and liquidity is one of the critical pieces required for that transition to reach its full potential," said Franklin Bi, General Partner at Pantera Capital. "Fission is building infrastructure that will help transform tokenized funds from representations of traditional products with legacy constraints into fundamentally more liquid and productive assets."
The round adds Pantera Capital, Circle Ventures, Borderless Capital and Ari Rubenstein to Fission's investor base, alongside existing backers including New Form, gumi Cryptos Capital, Anthony Scaramucci, Manhattan Venture Partners, Reflexive Capital and Lattice Capital.

Santander Builds AI Capabilities That Improve Performance and Lower Costs Using NVIDIA AI Infrastructure
summary:
Banco Santander today announced a new milestone in their artificial intelligence collaboration with NVIDIA. With support from NVIDIA, the Santander AI Lab has developed new capabilities to evaluate AI models and agents for banking applications, helping identify which model is best suited for each task and deploy it in the most efficient way.
The work is being carried out through Santander AI Lab, which explores and tests emerging AI technologies before broader deployment across the bank. As part of this effort, Santander has been progressively moving from large general-purpose models towards smaller, specialised models designed for specific banking tasks. In selected experimental use cases, this approach has reduced serving costs from around €5 per interaction to approximately €0.03 while maintaining strong performance.
Through the Lab, Santander has built Model Arena to evaluate open-weight models against banking tasks and identify the right model for each workload, and is specialising models using NVIDIA NeMo Customizer. Customer-service comparisons delivered evidence that smaller, specialised models can deliver strong performance on targeted banking tasks. Santander has built specialised intelligence for core banking workloads on NVIDIA Kumo, a family of open-weight foundation models for structured data, allowing companies to quickly turn structured data into predictive insights needed for agentic services.
The Lab is industrialising inference within Santander’s own architecture using NVIDIA Dynamo-Triton, the approach behind the serving-cost reduction above,  and is developing Model Arena to design, simulate, evaluate and supervise banking agents, alongside performance engineering and adversarial testing of conversational AI in controlled environments. The goal is to establish a rigorous experimentation path through which emerging AI technologies are optimised and stress-tested against banking requirements before successful capabilities scale across Santander.
Building on these advances, Santander is progressing from open-weight models towards specialised models and governed banking agents designed for greater control, safety and lower operating costs at scale. The collaboration is already delivering measurable results: in an experimental customer-service use case, Santander improved conversation quality while reducing costs by more than 50% through the deployment of a more efficient AI model.
As part of the next phase of the initiative, Santander and NVIDIA have established a three-year collaboration framework covering areas such as foundation models, AI agents, fraud and anti-money laundering capabilities, real-time decisioning and advanced simulation technologies, including a banking digital twin.
Iñaki Bernal, chief artificial intelligence officer at Santander, said: "NVIDIA is a key player in the infrastructure, software and research that is powering the latest advances in artificial intelligence. Combined with Santander's scale across businesses, customers and geographies, we believe we are uniquely positioned to succeed in transforming those advances into practical banking capabilities."
Aser Blanco, Global Banking Lead at NVIDIA, said: “Banking is one of the most data-centric industries. Data sits at the heart of every process and now banks need to become intelligence-centric. Transforming years of data into usable and proprietary intelligence is not about model size, but about training and fine tuning. In this new world, cost per intelligence output is a key metric. Santander is showing what that looks like in production with smaller models, specialised on the bank’s own data, evaluated against real banking tasks and served efficiently enough to run at the scale of a global bank.”

content: Banco Santander has announced new AI capabilities developed in collaboration with NVIDIA through the Santander AI Lab. By transitioning from general-purpose models to smaller, specialised models using NVIDIA infrastructure and software, the bank has significantly reduced operating costs while maintaining strong performance for banking applications. The companies have also established a three-year collaboration framework to further advance AI agents, fraud detection, and real-time decisioning technologies.

NVIDIA இன் உள்கட்டமைப்பு மற்றும் மென்பொருளைப் பயன்படுத்தி, பொதுவான மாடல்களில் இருந்து சிறிய மற்றும் பிரத்யேக மாடல்களுக்கு மாறுவதன் மூலம், வங்கி செயல்பாட்டுச் செலவுகளைக் கணிசமாகக் குறைத்துள்ளது. மேலும், AI ஏஜெண்டுகள் மற்றும் மோசடி கண்டறிதல் தொழில்நுட்பங்களை மேம்படுத்த இந்த நிறுவனங்கள் மூன்று ஆண்டு கூட்டுறவை எட்டியுள்ளன.
